mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations. This results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Core PCE inflation falls below 2% during the signal period, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into broad price inflation and thus will not trigger a hawkish Fed response.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3M change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: ISM Manufacturing PMI rises above 60 during the signal period, indicating that the supply chain disruption is transient and not materially impacting overall industrial activity.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed pivots to a dovish stance within 3 months of the signal, either by cutting rates or signaling a pause in the hiking cycle.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3M change > 10%), it signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 30Y mortgage rates rise above 6% during the signal period, indicating that housing affordability is deteriorating and will likely dampen the consumer spending impulse.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over 3 months, it signals a weakening labor market that will depress consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall below 200K during the signal period, indicating that the rise in unemployment is likely temporary and not signaling a broad labor market downturn.

mechanism_narrative: When the spread between the 10Y and 2Y Treasury yields inverts (10Y-2Y < 0), it signals a looming recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens (10Y-2Y > 1%) within 3 months of the inversion signal, indicating that the recession risk has abated.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales growth decelerates sharply (3M change < -5%), it signals a weakening consumer sector that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rises above 90 during the signal period, indicating that the consumer spending slowdown is likely temporary and not signaling a broad economic downturn.
